avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducer significantly reduces nevirapine plasma concentrations and antiretroviral efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid completely and report use

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin/Rifampicin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4/2B6 inducer decreases nevirapine levels by 20-40%, reducing antiviral activity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if tuberculosis treatment required, use alternative antiretroviral regimen

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce nevirapine concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; monitor viral load if used

caution_supplements.name: Echinacea
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 induction may modestly reduce nevirapine levels
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for maintained viral suppression

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 induction possible; limited clinical data in HIV patients
caution_supplements.action: Inform provider of use; monitor therapeutic response

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase nevirapine levels, potentially increasing toxicity risk (hepatotoxicity, rash)
avoid_foods.action: Advise patient to avoid grapefruit products during nevirapine therapy

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay nevirapine absorption slightly; no significant impact on bioavailability
caution_foods.action: May take with or without food; consistent timing improves adherence

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (high intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contain compounds that may induce CYP3A4; high intake may reduce nevirapine levels
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary consumption acceptable; excessive supplementation should be discussed with provider

monitoring_notes: Monitor liver function tests regularly as nevirapine carries risk of hepatotoxicity, particularly in first 18 weeks. Assess for drug interactions at each visit, especially with concurrent medications affecting CYP3A4/2B6, and emphasize importance of adherence for virological control.
